# Disagreement Log — Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 3

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Chapter:** SHE 003 — Vision 1, Chapter 3
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA

---

## Disagreements

### 1. V. 2 — "God of hosts" vs. "God of Hosts" vs. "God of all power"
- **EMET:** "God of hosts" (lowercase) — literal Sabaoth
- **LOGOS:** "God of Hosts" (capitalized title)
- **PNEUMA:** "God of all power" — dynamic rendering
- **Decision:** "God of Hosts" (LOGOS) — preserve traditional title; capitalized as divine designation

### 2. V. 2 — "ordinances" vs. "commandments" vs. "commandments"
- **EMET:** "ordinances" — more archaic, juridical
- **LOGOS/PNEUMA:** "commandments" — standard NT term for entolai
- **Decision:** "commandments" — consistent with NT usage of entolai throughout Shepherd

### 3. V. 3 — "heathen" vs. "Gentiles" vs. "unbelievers"
- **EMET:** "heathen" — older rendering of ethne
- **LOGOS:** "Gentiles" — standard NT rendering
- **PNEUMA:** "unbelievers" — interpretive
- **Decision:** "Gentiles" — preserves the ethnic-religious distinction; "unbelievers" is too interpretive

### 4. V. 3 — "touched my chest" vs. "touched my breast"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "touched my chest" / "touched my breast"
- **PNEUMA:** "touched my chest"
- **Decision:** "touched my chest" — "breast" sounds archaic; the gesture is one of blessing/confirmation

### 5. V. 4 — "Be manly" vs. "Be brave" vs. "Be strong" vs. "Be courageous"
- **EMET:** "Be manly, Hermas" — literal andrizo
- **LOGOS:** "Be brave, Hermas!"
- **PNEUMA:** "Be strong, Hermas!"
- **Decision:** "Be courageous" — captures the andrizo sense without the gendered literalism, while being stronger than "brave"

### 6. V. 1 — "terrible" vs. "awe-inspiring" vs. "overwhelming"
- **EMET:** "terrible" — deinon can mean "terrible/fearful/awesome"
- **LOGOS:** "awe-inspiring" — preserves the reverence without negativity
- **PNEUMA:** "overwhelming"
- **Decision:** "awe-inspiring" — deinos here is clearly the numinous rather than the threatening

**Total disagreements: 6**
